# RETRO: PR #13114

## What worked
- Asking a neutral question about the issue comment's counterclaim (whether try/catch intercepts the error) focused both reviewers on the material mechanism; both used versioned Qt source and the delayed-call suffix as a discriminator.
- Cross-examination turned a source-only Sol conclusion (moderate confidence) into an independent runtime confirmation with its own positive control, so every public claim is dual-sourced.

## Process deviations (retained, excluded where relevant)
- Opus: first capability probe ran `qml6 --version` without `--apptype core` (SIGABRT in sandbox, core limit read back 0). Kept as invalid `opus/rv-cap`, redone as `rv-cap2`. The brief stated the rule; the reviewer did not follow it on the first attempt.
- Opus: the Read tool on a file under `src/head` auto-loaded the repository's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, exceeding the 60-line aggregate bound. Improvement: tell reviewers to read worktree files through bounded `sed -n` rather than the Read tool.
- Opus: one `cut -c1-400` display of probe stderr; not presented as complete; full value checked from results.json.
- Sol: several early probe runs (`qt-probe-cases`, `-verbose`, `-rules`, `-warning`, `-compiled`) invalid or incomplete (qml6 core mode hid QML warnings; a link failure without -fPIC). Preserved and excluded; conclusions use only `qt-probe-compiled-2`.
- Sol's first pass completed in 4.9 minutes source-only; a runtime probe was only done after a targeted follow-up.

## Tooling notes
- `qml6 --apptype core` does not surface QML warnings to stderr in Sol's runs, while Opus captured them with `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1`. A shared review-tools recipe for capturing QML engine warnings headlessly would save time (feature request, not a confirmed bug).
- `node` is absent from the review.py sandbox PATH, so `bar-test.sh`'s `run_node_test` block cannot run there (feature request).

## Carry forward
- Put "use shell reads, not the Read tool, inside worktrees" in the brief's first-call rules.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** On Qt 6.11.2 (the version reported in #13011), the new `try/catch` blocks stop the `Cannot assign to read-only property "moduleName"` warnings that `injectProps()` produced for custom command modules. Writing to a `readonly` QML property from JavaScript throws an ordinary JS `TypeError` (`QObjectWrapper::setProperty` in qtdeclarative), and Qt only logs it when the exception escapes to the signal-handler or `Qt.callLater` boundary. This contradicts the note in the #13011 comment that `try/catch` cannot suppress the warning. Two isolated probes ran the verbatim base and head `injectProps` bodies against a target shaped like `CustomCommandModule`:

| | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Direct call from `onLoaded` | `TypeError` warning, handler stops early | No warning, handler runs to its end |
| `Qt.callLater(injectProps)` | Same warning with `(exception occurred during delayed function evaluation)` | No warning |
| Final `bar` / `moduleName` / `settings` | Injected `bar`; `moduleName` and `settings` keep their `entry`-derived values | Identical to base |
| Writable targets (`BarWidget`, `Panel`) | All three written | Identical to base |

A deliberately uncaught read-only write in the same harness still produced both warnings, so the logger and both reporting paths were live when the head version stayed silent. The new `bar-test.sh` assertion, evaluated on its own, is false against base `Bar.qml` and true against head.

### "Fixes #13011" claims a crash fix that is not established

The PR body links the warnings to the `QQuickRepeater::regenerate` SIGSEGV and closes #13011. The new test comment says a TypeError "took the shell down in #13011". For the only delegate that throws, head leaves exactly the same object state as base: the one runtime difference is that the exception is caught instead of logged. Qt clears the exception at the handler or delayed-call boundary, so nothing in the inspected source passes it to incubation or `DelegateModel` code. The crash frames in #13011 are a `typeof` name lookup and a property read inside `libQt6QmlModels`, not the read-only write path. The reporter also wrote that they could not confirm the warnings were the trigger.

**Impact:** The "Fixes" keyword would auto-close a crash report that has not been shown fixed, and the test comment would record an unproven cause as fact.

**Suggested change:** Use "Refs #13011" (or keep the issue open until the reporter confirms the crash is gone), and reword the test comment to something like "preceded a crash reported in #13011".

### Empty `catch` blocks also silence unrelated injection failures

Each `catch (e) {}` swallows any exception from its write, not only the read-only case. At base, an exception thrown inside `root.pluginBarApiFor(...)`, or a plugin or custom QML widget whose property type rejects the injected value, was logged. At head it fails silently; a failed `bar` write leaves the widget with its default `bar`. The PR description says a read-only declaration now "skips"; the write is still attempted on every load and settings change, and the resulting exception is caught.

**Impact:** Future plugin or custom-widget injection errors would produce no log output, making them harder to diagnose.

**Suggested change:** `ModuleSlot` already has `commandCustom`, which picks `CustomCommandModule` for the component loader. Skipping the two derived properties for that case avoids the read-only writes without catching anything else (untested sketch):

```qml
if ("bar" in target) target.bar = firstParty
  ? root : root.pluginBarApiFor(pluginApiId, moduleName, registered)
if (!commandCustom && "moduleName" in target) target.moduleName = moduleName
if (!commandCustom && "settings" in target) target.settings = moduleSettings
```

`BarModel.inlineSettingsDelta` already sends custom-module settings changes through a full rebuild, because those modules read `entry` directly, so skipping `settings` there loses no live-update path. This guard only covers the known command widget. A custom QML widget that declares its own read-only `moduleName` or `settings` would still log. Alternatively, keep the `try` blocks and log errors other than the read-only `TypeError`. Either way, the new `bar-test.sh` regex requires `try {` before each write, so it would need to match whichever guard is kept.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head and base, plus qtdeclarative v6.11.2 and Quickshell v0.3.1 source. Runtime evidence comes from two independent isolated Qt 6.11.2 QtQml harnesses that ran the verbatim `injectProps` bodies against synthetic targets, through both a direct handler call and `Qt.callLater`, with positive controls. Not tested: the full Quickshell shell, its `Loader`/`Repeater` structure, the SIGSEGV itself (no reproducer), and the full `bar-test.sh` suite (the "89 assertions" result was not rerun).

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, with claims cross-checked between them, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
